title: Student visa for the UK from Uzbekistan: step by step
summary: The steps from a sponsor's offer to the biometric appointment, with the current gov.uk maintenance and visa fee figures and a warning to recheck them on the day you apply.

sources.title: GOV.UK: student visa money (maintenance and fees)
GOV.UK: student visa eligibility and processing times

review_note: Verified on the fetched gov.uk student visa money page: maintenance £1,529 per month (London) and £1,171 per month (outside London) for up to 9 months; visa application fee £558 when applying from outside the UK. Verified on gov.uk/student-visa: eligibility (16+, offer from a licensed sponsor, English, financial requirement) and processing times (about 3 weeks from outside the UK, about 8 weeks from inside). Not verified: the Immigration Health Surcharge rate (the gov.uk page returned 404), the TB test country list (404), and a reported rise in maintenance from 30 November 2026 (seen only in third-party sources; the article tells readers to check gov.uk). Recheck every figure before publication.
body:
## In short

- To study in the UK you need a student visa, which you apply for from Uzbekistan through the UK government's visa application process.
- You must hold an offer from a licensed student sponsor, show that you can pay for your course and living costs, and meet the English requirement.
- Gov.uk sets the figures for the financial requirement and the visa fee. Check them on the day you apply, because they change.
- Processing times differ by where you apply from. Gov.uk currently says the typical decision time is about three weeks from outside the UK.

## Step 1: Get an offer from a licensed sponsor

Start with the university. You need an offer for a course at a university or college that is a licensed student sponsor. Without that, you cannot apply for a student visa. Once the university has confirmed your place and issued the document that sets out your course, you can start the visa application.

Ask the university to confirm three things in writing: the course start date, the course length and the fee. The visa application depends on these details matching.

## Step 2: Check the English requirement

Gov.uk states that you must be able to speak, read, write and understand English. The evidence you need depends on your circumstances, and a separate gov.uk page explains the accepted tests. Check the accepted test list before you book a test, because the list the government accepts for visa purposes can differ from the list a university uses.

## Step 3: Show your money

The financial requirement is the amount you must show that you have available to pay for your course and living costs. On gov.uk, the current maintenance figure for students in London is £1,529 a month and outside London is £1,171 a month, for up to nine months. Gov.uk also lists the visa application fee for applying from outside the UK as £558.

Some commercial sites report that these figures will rise from 30 November 2026. I could not confirm that on gov.uk when I checked, so check the official page on the day you apply. If the change applies to your application date, use the new figure, not the old one.

Rules also cover how long you must hold the money, the type of account, and the evidence you must provide. Read the official guidance for the exact evidence list. Do not assume that a bank statement from a family member is enough, and do not move money into your account just before you apply.

## Step 4: Check whether you need a TB test

Some applicants must take a tuberculosis test before a UK visa decision. Whether it applies depends on your country and on how long you will stay. Check the official government list for your country, and if the test is required, book it with an approved clinic. Do this early, because results can take time.

## Step 5: The health surcharge

Most students pay the Immigration Health Surcharge as part of the application. It is charged per year of your visa, so a longer course costs more. Gov.uk publishes the current rate, and you should check it on the official page before you calculate your budget.

## Step 6: Complete the online form and book a biometric appointment

Complete the online application, pay the fees and book a biometric appointment at a visa application centre. Bring your passport and the documents listed in the online form. Make sure the names on your documents match your passport exactly. A mismatch is one of the most common reasons for delay.

Gov.uk gives typical processing times. For an application from outside the UK, the usual decision time is about three weeks, and for an application from inside the UK it is about eight weeks. You may be able to pay for a faster decision where that service is available.

## Step 7: Plan your arrival

Check the start date for your course, and aim to arrive a few days before orientation. Keep copies of your visa, offer letter and financial evidence in case you are asked for them at the border. Register with your university on arrival and keep your attendance records, because sponsors have duties to report students who stop attending.

## Working while you study

Student visa holders can usually work part-time during term time and full-time during official holidays, within limits set by the visa conditions. Check the current conditions on gov.uk, because the limits can change. Do not rely on part-time work to pay for your course or your first months of living costs.

## Common mistakes

- Applying before you have a valid offer or confirmed course dates.
- Using an old financial figure from a blog.
- Paying for a service that the official form lets you do yourself.
- Forgetting the TB test or the biometric appointment, which can delay the decision.
- Mismatched names or dates across documents.

## Documents to gather before you apply

Put everything in one folder, and check each document against the list on the official online form. The usual items are a valid passport, the course offer from your sponsor, evidence of your financial requirement, evidence of your English level, your academic certificates and any TB test result if required. Keep the originals safe and bring them to the biometric appointment.

If a document is not in English, the form may require a certified translation. Check the official guidance for what counts as a valid translation, and ask the sponsor whether it has a standard translation template.

Your financial evidence must show the money you need, in the account type the rules accept, for the period the rules set. Keep the statements in order by date, and do not edit or redraw them. If an account is held by a relative, the rules about sponsor letters and relationships apply, so read them closely.

## Your application route and your family

If a dependant wants to join you, check the dependant rules before you apply. These are separate applications with their own financial evidence, and the rules can change. Do not assume that a family member can come simply because you can.

## Your first weeks in the UK

Plan your first week carefully. Confirm your travel, your accommodation and your university registration date. Ask the university to confirm the process for collecting your biometric residence permit, if one is required. Set up a UK bank account if you can, because a UK account makes rent and bills easier to manage. Keep your visa, offer letter and sponsor contact details in your phone and on paper.

## Keeping your visa in good standing

A student visa comes with conditions. Attend classes, keep your sponsor informed of changes to your course, and keep your contact details up to date. If you change course, leave the course early or defer, tell your sponsor, because the sponsor may have to report the change. Breaking the conditions can affect future applications, so ask the university's international office when you are unsure.

## When an application is refused

A refusal letter explains the reasons. Read it carefully and check whether you can reapply with new evidence. Some refusals can be challenged, and some can only be fixed by a new application. Get advice from the university's international office or a regulated immigration adviser before you pay for a new application.

## Checklist

- [ ] Confirm your offer and course dates with the licensed sponsor in writing.
- [ ] Check the English test list on gov.uk and book a test if needed.
- [ ] Check the current financial requirement on gov.uk on the day you apply.
- [ ] Check whether a TB test is required for your country.
- [ ] Check the current Immigration Health Surcharge rate.
- [ ] Pay the visa fee shown on gov.uk and keep the receipt.
- [ ] Book the biometric appointment and bring the documents listed.
- [ ] Keep copies of all documents for arrival and university registration.
